MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #11 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. If x = 10, what is the value of x ÷ 2 + 1? (1 mark)
   A. 5
   B. 11
   C. 6
   D. 1

2. Which pair are like terms? (1 mark)
   A. 4 and 4z
   B. 3a and 5b
   C. 2x and 2y
   D. 3a and 5a

3. What is 5 m 20 cm − 2 m 75 cm? (1 mark)
   A. 2 m 45 cm
   B. 2 m 35 cm
   C. 3 m 45 cm
   D. 2 m 55 cm

4. What is 3 m 45 cm + 2 m 80 cm? (1 mark)
   A. 5 m 25 cm
   B. 6 m 15 cm
   C. 6 m 25 cm
   D. 7 m 25 cm

5. A pencil starts at the 2 cm mark on a ruler and ends at the 9 cm mark. How long is the pencil? (1 mark)
   A. 8 cm
   B. 7 cm
   C. 9 cm
   D. 11 cm

6. A rectangle has an area of 36 square units and 4 rows. How many columns does it have? (1 mark)
   A. 40
   B. 32
   C. 9
   D. 10

7. A rectangle is made of 8 rows with 12 unit squares in each row. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 40 square units
   B. 104 square units
   C. 96 square units
   D. 20 square units

8. Wanjiku says the area of a rectangle with 4 rows and 6 columns is 10 square units. Her mistake is that she (1 mark)
   A. added instead of multiplying
   B. counted the corners
   C. forgot to use a ruler
   D. multiplied instead of adding

9. A cuboid is 6 blocks long, 3 blocks wide and 2 blocks high. What is its volume? (1 mark)
   A. 11 blocks
   B. 42 blocks
   C. 36 blocks
   D. 18 blocks

10. A cuboid has a volume of 100 blocks. One layer has 20 blocks. How many layers are there? (1 mark)
   A. 120
   B. 6
   C. 80
   D. 5

11. A cuboid has a volume of 60 blocks. One layer has 12 blocks. How many layers are there? (1 mark)
   A. 6
   B. 48
   C. 5
   D. 72

12. How many half-litre containers fill 1 litre? (1 mark)
   A. 3
   B. 1
   C. 2
   D. 4

13. What is capacity? (1 mark)
   A. The height of a container
   B. The colour of a container
   C. The amount of liquid a container can hold
   D. The mass of a container

14. How many 5 L buckets can be filled from a 20 L jerrycan? (1 mark)
   A. 15
   B. 4
   C. 5
   D. 2

15. What is 4 1/2 kg + 2 3/4 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 7 1/4 kg
   B. 7 3/4 kg
   C. 7 kg
   D. 7 1/2 kg

16. What is 7 1/2 kg − 2 3/4 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 4 3/4 kg
   B. 4 1/2 kg
   C. 5 1/4 kg
   D. 5 kg

17. What is 4 kg − 1/4 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 3 3/4 kg
   B. 4 kg
   C. 4 1/4 kg
   D. 3 1/2 kg

18. What is 6 h − 2 h 15 min? (1 mark)
   A. 3 h 55 min
   B. 3 h 45 min
   C. 3 h 35 min
   D. 4 h 45 min

19. Assembly starts at eight o'clock in the morning. How do we write this time? (1 mark)
   A. 8:00 p.m.
   B. 8:00 a.m.
   C. 8:30 a.m.
   D. 8:00 noon

20. How long is a lesson that starts at 8:15 a.m. and ends at 10:40 a.m.? (1 mark)
   A. 2 h 35 min
   B. 2 h 25 min
   C. 3 h 25 min
   D. 2 h 10 min

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. A ribbon is 5 m 20 cm long. A piece 2 m 75 cm long is cut off. How much ribbon is left? (3 marks)

22. Describe how the length of a shadow changes from morning to afternoon and explain how this can help us to estimate the time of day. (4 marks)

23. A square garden has sides of 15 m. Find the perimeter of the garden. (2 marks)

24. Simplify 2a + 5 + 3a + 1 and find its value when a = 4. (4 marks)

25. Wanjiru studied for 1 hour 20 minutes on Monday and 45 minutes on Tuesday. How long did she study in all? (3 marks)

26. Explain how you can use a beam balance to find the mass of a bag of sugar. (3 marks)

27. Wanjiku has 2 L of milk and buys 1 1/2 L more. How much milk does she have now? (2 marks)

28. Amina has a 3 L jug of water. She pours 1 1/4 L into a pot and 1/2 L into a cup. How much water is left in the jug? (4 marks)

29. Add 2 1/2 kg and 1 3/4 kg. Show your working. (3 marks)

30. The mass of a basket full of mangoes is 8 kg and the basket alone is 1 1/2 kg. Find the mass of the mangoes alone. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #11 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — 6
   Replace the letter by its value and work it out. The answer is 6.

2. D — 3a and 5a
   Like terms have the same letter. 3a and 5a both have the letter a.

3. A — 2 m 45 cm
   520 − 275 = 245 cm = 2 m 45 cm.

4. C — 6 m 25 cm
   Change to centimetres: 345 + 280 = 625 cm = 6 m 25 cm.

5. B — 7 cm
   Subtract the start from the end: 9 − 2 = 7 cm.

6. C — 9
   Rows × columns = 36, so columns = 36 ÷ 4 = 9.

7. C — 96 square units
   Area = rows × columns = 8 × 12 = 96 square units.

8. A — added instead of multiplying
   Area is 4 × 6 = 24 square units. She added 4 + 6.

9. C — 36 blocks
   One layer has 6 × 3 = 18 blocks. There are 2 layers, so the volume is 18 × 2 = 36 blocks.

10. D — 5
   Layers = 100 ÷ 20 = 5.

11. C — 5
   Layers = 60 ÷ 12 = 5.

12. C — 2
   Two halves make one whole.

13. C — The amount of liquid a container can hold
   Capacity tells us how much liquid a container holds when it is full.

14. B — 4
   20 ÷ 5 = 4 buckets.

15. A — 7 1/4 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 4 1/2 kg + 2 3/4 kg = 7 1/4 kg.

16. A — 4 3/4 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 7 1/2 kg − 2 3/4 kg = 4 3/4 kg.

17. A — 3 3/4 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 4 kg − 1/4 kg = 3 3/4 kg.

18. B — 3 h 45 min
   Change 1 hour to 60 minutes when the minutes are not enough. The answer is 3 h 45 min.

19. B — 8:00 a.m.
   Times from midnight to noon use a.m. and times from noon to midnight use p.m. The correct answer is 8:00 a.m..

20. B — 2 h 25 min
   Count on from 8:15 a.m. to 10:40 a.m.. The total is 2 h 25 min.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2 m 45 cm
   Working / marking points: 520 − 275 = 245 cm (2 marks); 245 cm = 2 m 45 cm (1 mark).

22. (4 marks)
   Answer: In the morning shadows are long, they get shorter towards midday when they are very short, and then get longer again in the afternoon. A very short shadow means it is about midday.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for long in the morning, 1 mark for short at midday, 1 mark for long again in the afternoon, 1 mark for estimating time.

23. (2 marks)
   Answer: 60 m
   Working / marking points: 15 + 15 + 15 + 15 = 60 m. 1 mark for method and 1 mark for answer with unit.

24. (4 marks)
   Answer: 5a + 6. When a = 4, 5 × 4 + 6 = 26.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 5a, 1 mark for 6, 1 mark for replacing a, 1 mark for 26.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2 hours 5 minutes
   Working / marking points: 20 + 45 = 65 min (1 mark); 1 h + 65 min = 2 h 5 min (2 marks).

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Put the sugar in one pan. Add known masses to the other pan until the beam is level. Add up the masses to find the mass of the sugar.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for putting the sugar in a pan, 1 mark for adding known masses until level, 1 mark for adding the masses.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: 3 1/2 L
   Working / marking points: 2 + 1 1/2 = 3 1/2. 1 mark for the addition and 1 mark for the unit.

28. (4 marks)
   Answer: 1 1/4 L
   Working / marking points: 1 1/4 + 1/2 = 1 3/4 L used (2 marks); 3 − 1 3/4 = 1 1/4 L (2 marks).

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: 4 1/4 kg
   Working / marking points: Wholes 2 + 1 = 3 (1 mark); parts 2/4 + 3/4 = 5/4 = 1 1/4 (1 mark); total 4 1/4 kg (1 mark).

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: 6 1/2 kg
   Working / marking points: 8 − 1 1/2 = 6 1/2. 1 mark for the subtraction and 1 mark for the unit.
